title: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 24](/bible/2-kings/24)

**[2 Kings 24:1-4](/bible/2-kings/24#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/24#v1)</sup> In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years: then he turned and rebelled against him.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/24#v2)</sup> And the Lord sent against him bands of the Chaldees, and bands of the Syrians, and bands of the Moabites, and bands of the children of Ammon, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by his servants the prophets.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/24#v3)</sup> Surely at the commandment of the Lord came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/24#v4)</sup> And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the Lord would not pardon.

- In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him.
- The Lord sent bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Judah to destroy it according to the word he spake by his prophets.
- This came upon Judah at the commandment of the Lord to remove them out of his sight for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed, which the Lord would not pardon.
  - **[Jeremiah 4:6](/bible/jeremiah/4#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/jeremiah/4#v6)</sup> Set up the standard toward Zion: retire, stay not: for I will bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.

    The Lord warned he would bring evil from the north, a great destruction, which is the army of Babylon that came against Judah.

**[2 Kings 24:5-7](/bible/2-kings/24#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/24#v5)</sup> Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/24#v6)</sup> So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers: and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his stead.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/24#v7)</sup> And the king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land: for the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt unto the river Euphrates all that pertained to the king of Egypt.

- Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
- The king of Egypt came no more out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that pertained to Egypt from the river of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
- Babylon took over as had been prophesied throughout the Bible, in Daniel and in Jeremiah, that Nebuchadnezzar would ransack Jerusalem and the surrounding lands.

**[2 Kings 24:8-12](/bible/2-kings/24#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/24#v8)</sup> Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. And his mother’s name was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/24#v9)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father had done.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/24#v10)</sup> At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/24#v11)</sup> And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants did besiege it.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/24#v12)</sup> And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers: and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

- Jehoiachin was eighteen years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done.
- The servants of Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jerusalem and besieged it, and the king himself came against the city while it was besieged.
- Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, princes, and officers, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

**[2 Kings 24:13-16](/bible/2-kings/24#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/24#v13)</sup> And he carried out thence all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, as the Lord had said.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/24#v14)</sup> And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/24#v15)</sup> And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king’s mother, and the king’s wives, and his officers, and the mighty of the land, those carried he into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/24#v16)</sup> And all the men of might, even seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths a thousand, all that were strong and apt for war, even them the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.

- Nebuchadnezzar carried out all the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and cut in pieces the vessels of gold Solomon had made, as the Lord had said.
- He carried away all Jerusalem, all the princes, all the mighty men of valour, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths, leaving only the poorest of the people of the land.
- He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry.
  - **[Isaiah 39:6](/bible/isaiah/39#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/isaiah/39#v6)</sup> Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.

    Isaiah prophesied to Hezekiah that all in his house and the treasures his fathers had laid up would be carried to Babylon, fulfilled in this robbing of the temple.

**[2 Kings 24:17-20](/bible/2-kings/24#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/24#v17)</sup> And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his father’s brother king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/24#v18)</sup> Zedekiah was twenty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/24#v19)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/24#v20)</sup> For through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

- The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
- Zedekiah was twenty one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all Jehoiakim had done.
- Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
  - **[Jeremiah 32:1-5](/bible/jeremiah/32#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/jeremiah/32#v1)</sup> The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/jeremiah/32#v2)</sup> For then the king of Babylon’s army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah’s house.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/jeremiah/32#v3)</sup> For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, Wherefore dost thou prophesy, and say, Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/jeremiah/32#v4)</sup> And Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes;
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/jeremiah/32#v5)</sup> And he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the Lord: though ye fight with the Chaldeans, ye shall not prosper.

    Jeremiah, shut up in prison, warned Zedekiah he would not escape but be delivered to Babylon, see the king face to face, and not prosper in fighting the Chaldeans.
